verdicts.evidence: KICKOFF.md lines 1052-1054: '*(only if regulated data or industry is in scope — GDPR/HIPAA/PCI/SOC2)*\nUse the compliance-auditor agent against the applicable regime, and the matching product-lane\nskill for framework detail — gdpr-ccpa-compliance or hipaa-compliance.' verified verbatim. SKILL.md line 3: 'description: Use when building a healthcare product that must comply with HIPAA — determining Business Associate status, handling PHI, implementing Security Rule safeguards, or preparing BAAs and breach response plans.' verified verbatim.
verdicts.reasoning: Two things here are things the skill cannot know: (1) the conditional gate — whether regulated data/industry is in scope for this specific milestone at all, and (2) the choice between two named sibling skills (gdpr-ccpa-compliance vs hipaa-compliance) for 'the applicable regime'. A skill's frontmatter description states when it SHOULD be invoked, but it has no mechanism to gate its own non-invocation or to arbitrate against a sibling skill covering a different regime — that decision is inherently the operator's / the compliance-auditor dispatcher's to make. This is squarely 'conditional gating the operator must judge' plus 'mode selection among modes/skills', both enumerated as NOT duplication. Survives.

verdicts.evidence: KICKOFF.md lines 1054-1056: 'Hand the auditor all\nthree of the things it establishes before it can map law to controls, rather than letting it\nguess them: which regulations actually apply' verified verbatim. SKILL.md line 125: '- HIPAA applicability assessment (Covered Entity vs. Business Associate vs. neither)' verified verbatim.
verdicts.reasoning: REFUTED as originally classified. The claim conflates two different-scope determinations. 'Which regulations actually apply' in the KICKOFF text is a multi-regime selection across the set named one clause earlier — GDPR/HIPAA/PCI/SOC2 — i.e. deciding WHICH of those four regimes govern this milestone at all, a decision that must be made BEFORE the operator can even pick 'the matching product-lane skill... gdpr-ccpa-compliance or hipaa-compliance' (chicken-and-egg: you need to know the regime to choose the skill, so the skill can't be the source of that answer). The hipaa-compliance skill's own deliverable at line 125, 'Covered Entity vs. Business Associate vs. neither', is a narrower HIPAA-INTERNAL sub-classification that presupposes HIPAA has already been identified as a relevant regime. These are not the same determination; the overlap is incidental phrasing ('applicability'/'applies') rather than a restatement of this skill's actual methodology. The instruction is also addressed to the compliance-auditor agent, a different asset, not to hipaa-compliance. Reclassified as load-bearing-parameter: regime-selection is project-specific scoping information the invoked skill cannot supply for itself, consistent with the sibling claim (hipaa-compliance-1) covering the same gating decision. Not a hit for this asset.

verdicts.reasoning: The skill defines what PHI IS (and enumerates the 18 identifiers at line 47) as a static reference taxonomy, but it has no way to know which of those categories THIS milestone's data actually falls into, where the affected users/data are jurisdictionally located, or where any prior audit history or policy docs live in this specific project. These are project-specific facts and pointers to prior artifacts — the canonical load-bearing category (per the rubric: 'which other artifact to feed in as context' and general project-specific parameters). Correctly classified; survives as load-bearing, not duplication.
